$$\mathrm{True}$$

The statement has no hypotheses, so the non-vacuity witness the gate asks for (step 7) is the trivial proposition, proved by `trivial`. It says nothing about the series.

$$\exists x \in \mathbb{R}\ \forall M \in \mathbb{N}\ \exists N \ge M\ \forall m \in \mathbb{Z}:\ N!\,x \ne m$$

The hypothesis of the criterion can hold: take $x = \sqrt{2}$ and $N = M$. Since $\sqrt 2$ is irrational and $M! \ne 0$, $M!\sqrt{2}$ is irrational, hence not an integer.

$$\exists N \in \mathbb{N}:\ 2 \le N$$

The one hypothesis of the statement, $2 \le N$, holds at $N = 2$.

$$\exists M \in \mathbb{N}:\ \mathrm{True}$$

The statement quantifies over $M$ with no hypothesis, so its witness is any natural number; $M = 0$ is used. It says nothing about the fractional parts.
